name: Load a tool into the VF-2's carousel through the spindle: Tnn and ATC FWD for an empty pocket, the holder pushed up into the spindle while Tool Release is held, then ATC FWD

working.role: takes each holder off the tool stand, carries it in and pushes it up into the spindle; the pendant's keys

steadying.role: holds the Tool Release button on the front of the spindle while the working hand seats the holder; otherwise rests at the side

phases.what: At the pendant, MDI, key in the first new tool's number (Tnn) and press ATC FWD: the tool in the spindle goes back to its pocket and pocket nn comes to the spindle, empty [proposed: force_n, duration_s; run in setup mode with the doors open]
phases.ends_on: the spindle empty, its tool number nn

phases.what: Standing in the doorway, a little further right for each fork further right, the working hand to the holder on the tool stand on the table, right of the vise, opening round its 1.25 in body under the flange [proposed: duration_s; the stance 72 mm right per fork, the reach one move of two overlapping parts]

Close the hand round the body, the flange resting on the index and thumb, firm the grip, take the holder's weight and lift it off the fork's tines [proposed: force_n, duration_s, travel_mm; 0.57 s from the fingers' contact to 2.5 mm up]

Slide it out of the fork toward the body, lift it clear of the part and the vise, carry it to about 3 in under the spindle, taper up and tool down, turning the grip about the holder's axis 10 deg for each fork further right, and line it up there [proposed: travel_mm, duration_s; longer from a farther fork, the grip's turn]
phases.ends_on: the holder under the spindle, on its axis

phases.what: The steadying hand's index up to the Tool Release button on the front of the spindle, waiting 30 mm off it [proposed: duration_s 1.65, was 0.8-1.0]

Push the holder up to under the drawbar; then hold Tool Release, which opens the drawbar, and push the holder on up into the spindle, pull stud first, until its taper stops it [proposed: force_n, duration_s; the index on the button 0.4 s after the holder stops under the drawbar]
phases.ends_on: the holder seated in the spindle's taper

phases.what: Let go of Tool Release: the drawbar pulls the holder in and holds it; then ease off it, open the hand and bring it back out and down to the side, clear of the holders still on the stand [proposed: duration_s 2.6, was 1.0]
At the pendant, ATC FWD: the carousel takes the tool into its pocket and turns the next pocket, empty, to the spindle; the next tool goes in the same way [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the tool in its pocket, the spindle empty

sources.ref: Haas Factory Outlet (Productivity Inc.), 'Haas Mill Operator' manual, rev. 8/2022, built from Haas's manuals with Haas's permission: the control keys (TOOL RELEASE, ATC FWD) and Changing Tools
sources.gives: TOOL RELEASE releases the tool from the spindle in MDI, Zero Return or Handle mode, and a button on the front of the spindle does the same; ATC FWD rotates to the next tool and makes a tool change, or to a tool entered (T1) first; tool changes may be made by hand with the tool release button on the spindle housing and ATC FWD and ATC REV, or in MDI with Tnn M6; tools go to the tool change position in Z by themselves; tools should always be loaded through the spindle, never directly into the tool changer

notes: The procedure for the VF-2's 20-pocket umbrella carousel. The pockets are the tools' numbers, given in the order the plan first uses them (moonshot/motion/tool_load.py: op10's five are T1-T5, op20's four T6-T9, op30's drill T10, op50's T11), the probe the shop's T20. The source gives the keys and the rule (load through the spindle with Tool Release, then ATC FWD); it gives no forces or times, and no hand for each job, so these are proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): which hand does what: the working hand carries the holder and seats it, as it is the hand the vf2-controls card gives the keys, so the steadying hand holds Tool Release, which the station has on the head's front left of the spindle (vf2.json tool_release_button); the tools waiting on a stand on the table right of the vise, its forks holding the holders by the V-flange, tool down (world/tooling.py STAND: no source gives where the shop stages tools; a cart beside the doorway is out of reach of a hand reaching forward to the spindle); 3 N on the keys and 5 N on the button (#1, #6, #8), the station's affordance forces; #1 4 s for MDI, the number's two or three keys and ATC FWD, done so rather than with an MDI Tnn M6 line and Cycle Start, which the source also gives; #2 0.32-0.67 s, the right hand's reach-to-grasp from the vise setup's footage (person.reach_to_grasp_right_s), borrowed as no footage of a tool load was found; #2 standing 72 mm further right for each fork further right, the stand's pitch, so the reach to every holder is the first's (from one place the reach to the third fork right was 54-108 mm longer and, kept inside people's reach time, still moving as the fingers closed, its grip loaded within 0.03-0.13 s, people's preload 0.14-0.32 s), and the reach planned as one move of two overlapping parts (Flash and Henis 1991), 0.46 s to in front of the holder and 0.24 s onto the grip from 0.32 s into it (as two moves one after the other the hand reached 31 m/s^2, past what the cause check allows); #3 the holder's weight, about 11-15 N, taken in people's grasp phases (Guillery 2013): the fingers on it 0.23 s before the hand takes any weight (preload), the weight taken and the grip firmed over 0.26 s, and the holder lifted 2.5 mm from 0.14 s into that over 0.2 s, 0.57 s in all, a holder heavier than 1.2 kg (the face mill's) lifted 0.33 s per kg sooner, as the arm comes up to its weight later; #4 68 mm out of the fork in 0.43 s, 200 mm up in 0.5 s, and in under the spindle in 1.2 s from the first fork, longer from a farther one (its peak acceleration kept), lined up there for 0.8 s, 2.9 s in all, the grip turned about the holder's axis 10 deg further for each fork further right (from a stance further right the arm reaches further across to the spindle, and with the grip unturned the wrist bent back 45-50 deg: from the fourth fork a median negative log-likelihood of 29.9 against people's 28.7, 28.2 turned 15 deg, 27.2 turned 30); #5 1.65 s for the longer reach up to the head, from 0.7 s before the holder reaches the spindle to 0.15 s after it is lined up, waiting 30 mm off the button, then in over 0.3 s (from 50 mm in 0.15 s it struck the button at 22 N, bounced off and pressed it twice); #6 Tool Release held about 1 s while the holder goes up the last 26 mm, the index on the button 0.4 s after the holder stops under the drawbar (pressed while the right hand pushed the holder up there, the trunk carried the left hand 20 mm across the head onto the button's edge); #7 2.6 s: the drawbar's fingers close in 0.35 s, the hand eases off in 0.25 s, opens its fingers most of the way in about 0.35 s and draws back along them toward the body in 0.45 s (moved right across the holder's front, the fingers dragged through it), and goes back down to the side in about 1.3 s by way of a point above and in front of the hand's rest, high over the holders still on the stand and in front of the vise's crank; #8 0.5 s. The hands hang at rest a little lower and further out than the other takes' (motion/tool_load.py REST_MM), where people's straight-armed hang fits. Tool Release only releases with the spindle stopped, in MDI or handle jog (the source's Zero Return mode isn't modelled). The changer's own cycle (the source's tool change position in Z, the carousel turning) isn't simulated: each change happens across the cut to the next take. Not done here, as the plan has no step for it: measuring each tool's length on the tool setter (vf2-tool-setter), which a shop would do once its tools are in.
